title: Best note apps for UK students, tested on real coursework
metaDescription: We tested note apps on a 4,200-note vault and on real coursework, with UK prices checked this month and student discounts noted where they exist.
excerpt: Every app here was used for at least two weeks on real coursework. Prices are UK prices, checked this month, and we say when a student discount exists.
_note: EXAMPLE pillar page. A pillar links out to the cluster of reviews underneath it.

sections.heading: How we chose these apps
sections.body:
Every app on this page was used for at least two weeks on real coursework, not demoed for an afternoon. Each one was tested with the same 4,200-note vault so the search timings can be compared directly.

We pay for our own subscriptions. Where an app offers a student discount we say so, and the price shown is what you would pay in the UK on the date given.

sections.heading: What actually matters for coursework
sections.body:
Three things, in this order. Can you get your notes out again, because degrees last longer than apps do. Does search work on a few thousand notes, since that is what a year of lectures produces. Does it sync without losing edits when you are on a train with no signal.

Handwriting, templates and AI summaries are further down the list. Test the three above first.

picks.oneLiner: Searched 4,200 notes in 0.4 seconds, but budget for the paid plan.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for a note app as a student?
faq.a: No. Plain Markdown files in a synced folder cost nothing and are the safest option for keeping your notes long term. Pay only when search or sync on a free plan starts getting in your way.
